claim: Provinciaal Groendomein Hertberg in Herselt (Diestsebaan 28a, just south of Westerlo) is open daily from one hour before sunrise to one hour after sunset, dogs must be leashed except in designated off-leash zones, and the site offers walking, mountain biking, horseback riding and guided nature walks
quote: Hertberg is situated in Herselt at Diestsebaan 28a, 2230 Herselt... from one hour before sunrise to one hour after sunset... Dogs must be leashed, except in designated off-leash zones

claim: Hertberg was part of Prince de Merode's estate until 2004, sits on the De Merode walking-node network, hosts a children's nature-experience trail 'Stoerparcours' (ages 10-14), and may have some route interruptions through 1 April 2026 due to works
quote: Tot 2004 maakte Hertberg deel uit van de uitgebreide eigendommen van Prins de Merode... Wees alert in de periode 01/04/2024 - 01/04/2026

claim: Wandelnetwerk de Merode is the largest walking-node network in the area, spanning 700 km of marked paths across three provinces with red-and-white knooppunt signs, with abbeys of Tongerlo and Averbode both on the network
quote: 700 kilometer wandelpaden... de abdijen van Tongerlo en Averbode

claim: Westerlo tourism office promotes the De Merode network plus a signature 'Wandelen langs kastelen en water' route (castles-and-water walk), a wheelchair/buggy-accessible 'Wandelen op wieltjes' route, the GR5 long-distance trail, and a dog off-leash area at Beeltjens/Kwarekken
quote: Water and Castles Walk... GR 5 Long-Distance Trail... Accessible Walking Route (Wandelen op wieltjes)... Dog Off-Leash Area (Hondenlosloopweide)

claim: De Beeltjens en Kwarekken is a 127-hectare nature/castle park a few hundred meters from Westerlo's market square, featuring a star pattern of tree-lined paths laid out in the early 18th century by Jan Philips Eugeen de Merode and the 24m-high Asberg sand dune
quote: De Beeltjens en Kwarekken covers 127 hectares, just a few hundred meters from the market square... the Asberg, a sand dune 24 meters high

claim: Kasteel de Merode in Westerlo is an inhabited water castle set in a ~60-hectare wooded park with ponds, lawns and tree-lined avenues; the grounds are not freely accessible but open during events such as the Historalia outdoor spectacles
quote: The Kasteel de Merode is inhabited and therefore not freely accessible. However, the castle and park are only accessible during events such as the outdoor spectacles of Historalia

claim: Averbode Bos en Heide is a 593-hectare European 'top nature' reserve straddling Vlaams-Brabant, Limburg and Antwerpen with two marked routes (Blue ~4.3 km / 60 min and Red ~11.2 km / 170 min) starting at Averbode Abbey; paved dreven are wheelchair-accessible, dogs on leash, no swimming or picnicking in ponds
quote: Blue route: approximately 4.3 km (60 minutes)... Red route: approximately 11.2 km (170 minutes)... De verharde dreven zijn toegankelijk voor rolstoelgebruikers... Honden zijn welkom aan de leiband

claim: Provinciaal Groendomein Prinsenpark Retie is a 215-hectare mosaic of forests, meadows and water features in the Antwerp Kempen, freely accessible from one hour before sunrise to one hour after sunset, with sanitary facilities open daily 06:00-23:30; nature-management works run January-March 2026
quote: Prinsenpark is a beautiful domain of 215 hectares... freely accessible from one hour before sunrise to one hour after sunset... From January to March 2026, extensive nature management work will be conducted

claim: Provinciaal Recreatiedomein Zilvermeer in Mol (a swim-lake recreation domain ~25 km east of Westerlo) charges €6 standard entry but offers free-access days in 2026 including the Easter weekend 4-6 April and the open-doors day on 24 May 2026
quote: General access to Zilvermeer costs 6 euros... Easter Weekend (April 4-6, 2026): The recreational domain in Mol offers free access for three days

claim: Zilvermeer's day-recreation parking is free at P1 and P2 on Zilvermeerlaan, with 555 free uncovered bike-parking spots, accessible from cycling-node points 14 and 50; address Zilvermeerlaan 2, 2400 Mol
quote: Free parking is available at P1 and P2 locations on Zilvermeerlaan... Free bike parking with 555 uncovered spaces; accessible via cycling route nodes 14 and 50

claim: Het Olens Broek is a ~185-hectare green/blue ribbon of alder swamp forest, meadows, river dunes and hedgerows along the Kleine Nete near Olen, bordered on the north by the Kempense Heuvelrug sand dunes, and lies within 5 km of nature reserves Zwart Water, Mosselgoren, De Zegge, Neerhelst and Snepkensvijver
quote: approximately 185 hectares in size... bounded by the Kleine Nete and by the sand dunes of the Kempense Heuvelrug... within a radius of five kilometers lie the Flemish nature reserves Zwart Water, Kempense Heuvelrug and Mosselgoren and the reserves De Zegge, Neerhelst and Snepkensvijver

claim: The Zwart Water & Snepkensvijver suggestion-loop near Herentals takes walkers through marshes, fens, forest and heath, with Snepkensvijver being one of Flanders' oldest nature reserves and one of the last wet heathlands in the Kempen
quote: a refreshing hike along marshes, forests and heath... Snepkensvijver invites you for a welcome break, as one of the last wet heathlands in the Kempen

claim: The wandelknooppunt.be planner lists multiple Westerlo/Tongerlo starting points where walkers can build custom routes on the De Merode node network, with the Abdij van Tongerlo and the youth hostel Boswachtershuis as named trailheads
quote: Toerisme Westerlo, the Abdij van Tongerlo, and the youth hostel Boswachtershuis being ideal starting points
